draft.title: Feeling safe and connected
card: Liveability is how well a place meets the needs of the people who live there. Some of those needs are about feelings, not just buildings and services.
people who feel safe in their streets, homes and public spaces tend to rate their place as more liveable.
people who feel welcome and have friends, neighbours or groups nearby tend to rate their place as more liveable.
People who feel left out or threatened tend to rate the same place lower. Two people in the same suburb can rate it differently.
draft.remember: People tend to rate a place higher when they feel safe and connected, and lower when they feel left out or threatened.

a.q: Which change would most likely make Year 7 student Aroha rate her new town as more liveable?
opts: She joins a local netball team and makes friends
She finds out the town has a larger land area
She sees that the town was founded long ago
She notices the town has more streets than before
a.why: Joining a team helps her feel included and connected to others, and these feelings raise how people rate a place. The other options are facts about the town, and they say nothing about how safe, included or connected she feels.
a.clue: Think about how Aroha feels, not facts about the town.

b.q: Two families live on the same street in Darwin. One rates it as highly liveable. The other rates it low. Which reason best explains the difference?
opts: The second family feels left out by neighbours
The second family lives on a different street
The first family has a bigger house than the second
The first family lives closer to the city centre
b.why: People rate a place on how safe, included and connected they feel, so feeling left out can lower a rating even in the same place. Living on a different street does not fit, because both families live on the same street.
b.clue: The street is the same, so look at how each family feels.

a.best: She joins a local netball team and makes friends

b.best: The second family feels left out by neighbours

problems.detail: The clue ('Think about how Aroha feels, not facts about the town') gives the answer away. Only one option is about feelings, so it rules out the other three without the student needing to know the idea.
The clue ('look at how each family feels') gives the answer away. Only one option is about feelings, so a student can pick it without understanding the idea.
Why (a) says these feelings 'raise how people rate a place', stated as certain, but the card says people 'tend to' rate a place higher. It should keep the hedge, for example 'tend to raise'.

a.q: Which change would most likely make Year 7 student Aroha rate her new town as more liveable?
opts: She joins a local netball team and makes friends
She stops going to the park after being teased there
She feels unsafe walking home past an empty lot
She is left out of a group chat by her classmates
a.why: Joining a team helps her feel included and connected to others, and these feelings tend to raise how people rate a place. Being teased, feeling unsafe or being left out are also feelings, but they tend to lower her rating, not raise it.
a.clue: Does each change bring her closer to others or push her away?

b.q: Two families live on the same street in Darwin. One rates it as highly liveable. The other rates it low. Which reason best explains the difference?
opts: The second family feels left out by its neighbours
The first family feels unwelcome at the local club
The second family has made many friends nearby
Both families feel safe walking along the street
b.why: Feeling left out tends to lower how people rate a place, so it explains why the second family rates the street low. Feeling unwelcome would lower the first family's rating, which is the wrong way round, and a feeling both families share cannot explain a difference.
b.clue: Which reason would lower one family's rating but not the other's?

a.best: She joins a local netball team and makes friends

b.best: The second family feels left out by its neighbours
